Mochi 1 preview on Mac: files, RAM and published times

Mochi 1 preview is a 10B-parameter text-to-video model from Genmo built on an Asymmetric Diffusion Transformer. It generates 480p video and is a research preview, and one complete Mac measurement exists, on a 64 GB M4 Max.

Genmo · Updated 2026-10-24
Answer

Mochi 1 preview runs on a Mac with 64 GB or more. A published run on M4 Max · 64 GB used the Official Diffusers BF16 variant build (source, 2026-09-02).

Does it fit your NVIDIA GPU's VRAM?

Runs · Stated means the linked model card, app maker or NVIDIA says a GPU with that much VRAM runs the model; Runs · Published names the card of a dated run. Fits with offload means the main model weights fit in VRAM with a 15% margin but the full set does not: the text encoder and VAE run from system RAM, which is slower. Exceeds VRAM means even the main weights are too large for the card. Mac runs never count here.

Which Mac software routes are listed?

  • ComfyUI

    Official

    Formats: safetensors, gguf. Memory policy: component stages stay resident.

    On Apple Silicon ComfyUI runs on PyTorch MPS, not MLX. GGUF files need the separate city96/ComfyUI-GGUF custom node. Resident size is the sum of the weights, an upper bound: ComfyUI can unload models between stages and publishes no per-model Mac peak.

    Sources: ComfyUI README · ComfyUI system requirements · ComfyUI CLI arguments · ComfyUI-GGUF README

  • Diffusers

    Official

    Formats: safetensors, gguf. Memory policy: component stages stay resident.

    Runs on the PyTorch mps device on Mac and CUDA on NVIDIA. GGUF loads through from_single_file on the model class, not the pipeline. Resident size is the sum of the weights, an upper bound.

    Sources: Diffusers MPS guide · Diffusers GGUF guide

What does the official configuration say?

"Official Diffusers BF16 example: 22GB VRAM (CUDA). Single-GPU operation of the genmo harness needs about 60GB VRAM. No Mac statement."

Source: Mochi 1 model card · Read 2026-10-24.

What known issues should you check?

  • Known issue 1

    The only complete Mac measurement ran with 19.8 GB of swap on a 64 GB machine.

    Source: Zenn: Mochi 1 on M4 Max 64GB · Read 2026-10-24

  • Known issue 2

    The official card calls Mochi 1 a living and evolving checkpoint under the research preview, with 480p output.

    Source: Mochi 1 model card · Read 2026-10-24

Frequently asked questions

Can a 64 GB Mac run Mochi 1?

It completed, but slowly. Diffusers MochiPipeline with the bf16 variant on an M4 Max with 64 GB took 8940.3 s for 848x480, 84 frames and 64 steps. Peak unified memory reached 94.5 GB, and 19.8 GB of swap was reported.

What does the official card say about memory?

The card says single-GPU operation needs about 60GB VRAM, the full-precision Diffusers example needs 42GB and the BF16 example needs 22GB. These are CUDA figures for different configurations, not a Mac minimum.
